newsitem.title: USA: King assassin's health improves; gun test delayed.
newsitem.headline: King assassin's health improves; gun test delayed.

text.p: James Earl Ray, convicted assassin of civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr., was upgraded to fair condition Monday in his battle against terminal liver disease.

Columbia Nashville Memorial Hospital said Ray, 69, was admitted Saturday in serious condition but had improved slightly Monday. He has been in and out of the same hospital repeatedly since late last year.

Officials in Memphis have postponed a test firing of the rifle allegedly used to kill King 29 years ago in that city, a gun Ray contends could actually prove his innocence. Shelby County Criminal Court Judge Joseph Brown last week granted a delay in the test, originally scheduled for Monday, to give Ray's lawyers and prosecutors more time to work out details.
In February Brown cleared the way for the test by recommending that a state appeals court take up the matter. That court later gave its approval. Members of King's family also backed the test.

Ray, who confessed to the killing but later denied it, is serving a 99-year prison sentence. He has been trying to re-open the case and win a trial. His lawyers contend that tests on the gun would justify that by showing it was not the murder weapon.

The rifle was found tossed in the doorway of a shop near the motel where King was shot. Ray's lawyers have said it was a "throw down" gun and not the actual murder weapon and that Ray was only a pawn in a larger plot to kill King.
Previous test firings on the rifle by the FBI and by congressional investigators were not convlusive.
